full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite-party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 20-4-2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No.43 of 2010 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 28-1-2010 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna Sadar in Title Suit No. 153 of 2005 should not be set-aside. 

 5. The trial Court below after closing of the evidence and hearing argument of the parties by its judgment and decree dated 28-1-2010 decreed the suit declaring the termination of the plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 is illegal, irregular, without jurisdiction and the plaintiff is to be treated still in service and will get all the benefits including salary and allowances. 

 6. The defendant-petitioner, thereafter preferred Title Appeal No. 43 of 2010 against the said judgment and decree dated 28-1-2010 before the learned District Judge, Khulna. Eventually, the said appeal was transmitted to the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna, who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 20-4-2011 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court dated 28-1-2010. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 20-4-2011, the present defendant-petitioner, Aftabuddin Ahmed, Executive Director, UCEP moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 8. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that both the Courts below having failed to consider that the plaintiff-opposite-party by accepting his termination received all the salary, allowances and benefit without any objection and thus, he had no scope to file the suit challenging his termination and, as such, the Court of appeal below in affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court below committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He next submits Judgments of both the Courts below are based on misreading and non-consideration of the evidence and materials on record inasmuch as, it is apparent from the record that in complying with the provision of 7.51 of UCEP Service Rules, 2004 show cause notice was issued to the plaintiff and after considering the recommendation of inquiry committee the authority passed the order of termination and there was no illegality and irregularity in passing the said order and, as such, impugned judgment and decree is bad in law and it has occasioned failure of justice. 

 9. Mr AF Hassan Ariff, the learned Advocate while elaborating his argument referred to UCEP Service Rules, 2004 and submits that the appointment of plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 was not at all on regular basis and, as such, as per provision of Rule 1.2 of the UCEP Service Rules, 2004 the plaintiff cannot avail any protection of the said service Rules and thus, in affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court based on the misinterpretation of the service rule the learned judge of the lower appellate Court committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further upon referring to the written statements of the defendant petitioner submits that the plaintiff-opposite-party was appointed in 1983 on contact basis and after expiry of the contact period the plaintiff was again appointed on 30-9-1986 purely on temporary basis and the terms No. 6 of the appointment clearly stipulates that the service of an employee can be terminated at any time with one month salary of the notice period and since the plaintiff was paid the salary of notice period which duly accepted by him so the termination was quite legal and thus, the Court of appeal below in passing the impugned judgment of affirmance committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 16. Now, let me consider the main argument of Mr. Hassan Ariff that the Courts below having failed to consider that since the terms and conditions of plaintiffs service were not regulated by any legal instrument, it is not possible in law to grant a decree against an unwilling master that the plaintiff is still in service under him and, as such, both the Courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
